summary: The direct Global HSL mask cache can keep old coverage after an upstream Whites edit.
evidence: The key drops FILM_RESPONSE_ENABLED..GRAIN_SEED_LOW, which also contains WHITES, TONE_LIMITER, TONE_KNEE, TONE_GREY and TONE_PEAK. toneZonesWgsl reads these before applyHsl. With an unchanged source and HSL recipe, encodeHslSelection therefore reuses old coverage if only omitted slots change. Local GPU hue leaves use the same identity. A Node-only run of the checked-in key function with the actual parameter indices confirmed that Whites 0 → +0.5 leaves the key unchanged while Exposure changes it.
proposed_fix: Replace exclusion ranges with explicit upstream dependencies shared by Global HSL and Local hue selection. Do not change selection math.
check: Prime a non-neutral HSL recipe, move only Whites on the same direct source, and compare the settled picture with a forced cold selection at the identical final grade. Repeat with a Local hue mask.
notes: Patch intentionally not written in Phase 2.

summary: The picker synchronizes the same global edit state twice before sending one post-release sampling request.
evidence: hslPickSamples awaits syncGlobalEditState then calls hslFetchStage, which awaits syncGlobalEditState and editCommandQueue again. Pointer moves only collect coordinates, so there is no GPU readback or backend request per pointer move.
felt_impact: Unmeasured; likely below the 15 ms audit floor when clean. Retaining one save fence is more important than eliminating this small duplicate.
proposed_fix: Keep one guarded save and revision fence in hslFetchStage; trace whether it saves any actual work first.
check: Add a picker release-to-colour-selected probe alongside the HSL own-control step; use hsl-picker-speed.js for coverage.

summary: Tiled HSL rebuilds selection from scratch for every tile even during HSL slider edits that do not change coverage.
evidence: Main and Clarity tile calls pass no prepareKey, unlike the direct route. Each tile encodes the fields pass, four preparation dispatches and three selection dispatches for a one-layer recipe without edge shaping; output storage is overwritten by the next tile.
felt_impact: Unmeasured; highest potential on warm HSL saturation drags forced to tiled rendering. A material gain is plausible if the selection passes dominate, but persistent mask storage could be worse on the Neo.
proposed_fix: Measure the direct and tiled routes separately, then assess bounded visible-tile mask reuse keyed by source generation, upstream grade, region and mask settings. Do not retain full-frame scratch.
check: HSL own Saturation drag at Fit on both photos; add large/100% or forced tiled only if Fit does not exercise it. Compare first feedback, settle and peak memory.

summary: Show selection repeats CPU guide preparation and PNG transfer after range changes and even after edits that leave coverage unchanged.
evidence: renderHslPanels keys refresh on editRevision/globalEditGeneration, and hslEnd submits a detailed request even when only hue, saturation or luminance changed. hslDrainSelection serializes requests, so release can wait behind one obsolete draft. sample_stage caches only upstream RGB, then redoes selection preparation, selection, PNG/base64 and browser decode.
felt_impact: Unmeasured; removing a needless refresh eliminates the whole overlay wait and contention for that edit. For actual range changes the saving is the prepare share plus any obsolete draft still in flight.
proposed_fix: Key refreshes on visible selection inputs, not every grade revision. Reuse prepared data only for the same stage identity, region and scale within the existing memory allowance.
check: Extra HSL own-control probe with Show selection enabled: change Saturation, wheels and Vignette (no request expected); then Range/Feather and Exposure (refresh expected). Compare release-to-exact overlay and the prepare/select/encode breakdown.

summary: Global HSL picking and Show selection sample the un-denoised picture even when the rendered HSL selects the denoised one.
evidence: sample_stage uses cache.hsl_stage_input, which calls capture_stage_input from raw proxies without a source_filter; the direct GPU fields pass binds sourceProxy after Denoise resolution and tiled HSL uses the denoised tile. The sample request carries adjustments but no Denoise selection state. In noisy or heavily cleaned regions the selected hue and mask can differ.
proposed_fix: Resolve which Denoise source/approximation the picker should represent and share that identity with the selection endpoint; no additional GPU readback on the drag path without evidence.
check: Compare Show selection and a strong HSL luminance grade on the same noisy crop with Denoise off/on; verify the picker tracks what the grade actually selects.
notes: Patch intentionally not written in Phase 2.

summary: Turning HSL off does not release its large, grow-only GPU work textures.
evidence: Per-canvas direct and tiled engines retain capacity up to their largest width, height and layer count; disabling HSL returns before ensure and leaves allocations alive. releaseHslSelection is on transient-resource teardown. A one-layer engine holds 80 bytes per work pixel plus coarse data (about 320 MB at 4 megapixels), and each additional layer adds 16 bytes per pixel.
felt_impact: Unmeasured; mostly a memory-headroom benefit, potentially avoiding slower routes under pressure. No expected speedup for a warm HSL-on frame by itself.
proposed_fix: Measure residency and route changes first; release inactive scratch under pressure or after an idle delay, keeping resources alive until fenced.
check: HSL own eye on/off and warm Denoise toggle at large/Fit; inspect idle GPU bytes and route before ON, after OFF and after re-enable. The interleaved OFF timings are not a cold-memory baseline.

summary: A nonzero Black & White mix adds 25 neighbouring texture reads per pixel before the normal grade, even when only Exposure or Contrast is being dragged.
evidence: The guided path samples a clamped 5×5 source lattice, then runs the upstream colour/tone prefix for the pixel and its guide. HSL fields repeats it in its own pass when stacked. With B&W neutral or off, the guide is skipped. Denoise changes the source the guide reads.
felt_impact: Unmeasured; a warm guide reuse could remove most of the incremental B&W cost on Exposure/Contrast or Reds drags if texture loads dominate; a Denoise source swap is a legitimate miss.
proposed_fix: Compare the existing fused path with source-keyed guide reuse only if material. Preserve the same tap ordering and do not grow the memory budget; measure before any separate pass.
check: B&W Exposure/Contrast ON vs OFF, Reds own drag, and Denoise toggle on/off. Separate warm render cost from first guide computation and check settled pixel parity.

summary: The shared-mask shader still evaluates each pixel's analytical hue-range coverage even when only the shared mask is used.
evidence: applyHsl loops all ranges, evaluates smoothsteps and creates circular target vectors, then replaces weight with hslSharedCoverage. With shared selection and Uniformity 0, the loop serves neither coverage nor target. CPU _apply_recipe_strip similarly computes full analytical weights and Oklab for every active channel before replacing weights.
felt_impact: Unmeasured; likely below the audit floor for an isolated one-range seed, but the saving scales with active channels and up to 32 ranges per channel on every Exposure/Contrast and Denoise render.
proposed_fix: Skip analytical coverage when the shared mask supplies it and skip target computation when Uniformity is zero; preserve the fallback and exact hue arithmetic. Consider a matching CPU cleanup separately.
check: HSL own Saturation and Exposure/Contrast ON/OFF at Fit with the normal seed and a separate multi-range stack, then the existing HSL preview/delivery pixel checks.

summary: Dragging a wheel puck updates every grade control on every pointer move and bypasses the normal gesture pacing.
evidence: The puck handler calls syncControlsFromState (including geometry, all ranges and Vignette layout) synchronously, then invalidates/schedules the preview without beginInteraction or endInteraction. Native ranges and HSL wheel handlers bracket their drags. pacedPreviewInteraction requires interacting to preserve a frame when HSL or Denoise are stacked.
felt_impact: Unmeasured; isolated drag gain may be under 15 ms, but with HSL or Denoise stacked, proper pacing could prevent missed feedback during the drag. Test separately from the Blending slider.
proposed_fix: Synchronize only the current wheel fields and modified indicators per frame. Bracket the actual pointer capture lifetime with existing preview pacing, and separately verify single-gesture undo before changing history semantics.
check: Native Shadows puck own-control drag at Fit; add a stacked HSL or Denoise pass, compare first feedback and settled output, and verify one Undo restores the initial puck.

summary: The Vignette outline does layout reads when hidden and rebuilds both paths even when Amount does not change the shape.
evidence: renderVignetteShape reads pane and image rectangles before its visibility test. The group input listener unconditionally calls it, and a visible outline generates two 96-point SVG paths per event, though Amount and highlight protection do not enter their coordinates.
felt_impact: Unmeasured; likely below 15 ms in isolation, with most potential on repeated visible-overlay Amount moves. No extra preview texture or GPU pass was found.
proposed_fix: Short-circuit hidden state before layout and separate positioning from path updates keyed by the geometric inputs only.
check: Vignette Amount own drag with overlay off and on; check same outline and current geometry while moving Midpoint or the centre.

summary: Active Color recomputes the same primaries matrix even when the changed control cannot affect the matrix.
evidence: Color activation from tint or Saturation calls rgbPrimariesAdjustmentMatrix during every buildParams, as do unrelated Exposure/Contrast renders. The matrix depends only on the eight hue/purity fields, not tint, temperature or saturation. Colour itself is a fused pointwise shader path, not a rebuilding LUT or an extra pass.
felt_impact: Unmeasured; likely below the audit floor. Only consider if buildParams is hot in a real trace.
proposed_fix: Reuse the exact same computed nine floats for unchanged primaries using a tiny bounded memo or last-value cache. Do not replace it with a different numerical shortcut.
check: Color own Saturation and Exposure/Contrast ON/OFF at Fit. Profile buildParams and verify identical packed values after an unrelated change.

summary: The Color seed is rejected because tint 8 exceeds the backend maximum of 2.
evidence: applyChanges sends the complete adjustment state to the backend. Model validation rejects tint 8. A replacement with saturation +0.45, tint +0.40 and temperature 4500 K changed at least one display channel by over 2 percentage points in 10.3% of Canon and 29.5% of Sony 480px CPU proxy pixels.
proposed_fix: Seed saturation .45, tint .40 and white_balance_kelvin 4500. Keep the Color eye and use a native Saturation drag as primary; Temperature or Tint can be secondary.
check: Phase 3 Fit on IMG_7723.CR3 and DSC00636.ARW. Require acknowledged seed and distinct fresh settled ON/OFF signatures. CPU proxy display is only a visibility sanity check.

summary: The current tint-only Wheels seed produces a weak signature on both photos, and Blending misses the actual wheel gesture.
evidence: The stock seed had p95 maximum-channel change of only 0.9/0.7 display points on Canon/Sony CPU proxies. Adding Shadows +0.40 EV and Highlights +0.35 EV moved 77.2%/56.0% of proxy pixels by over 2 points. The existing canvas drag helper is hard-wired to the curve editor.
proposed_fix: Seed Shadows hue 220°, saturation 28%, luminance +0.40 EV and Highlights hue 38°, saturation 18%, luminance +0.35 EV. Keep the Wheels eye. Drag the Shadows puck from its live centre by a fixed offset using the existing trusted-pointer timing path with a wheel-specific drag geometry. Keep Blending as a fallback, labelled as such.
check: Run both photos at Fit, confirming settled ON/OFF signatures and actual hue/saturation movement at the end of the native puck drag.

summary: The HSL recipe uses an invalid hue_shift property and the legal part of the red-only seed is too narrow for these photos.
evidence: seed merges hue_shift into the live recipe but both shader packing and the UI use hue; backend HSLRecipe forbids extra keys. The legal default-red/Saturation +48 seed changed neither 480px proxy by over 2 display points. The proposed broad recipe did so on 57.9% of Canon and 36.4% of Sony pixels.
proposed_fix: Keep channel red with one broad range {center:110,width:155,feather:24,subtract:false}, hue:12, saturation:48, luminance:.75, default spatial settings. Acknowledge the recipe before measuring. Keep the HSL eye; use native Saturation drag to exercise reuse and a separate range handle drag with Show selection on to exercise mask updates.
check: Run both photos at Fit and check first feedback, settle and ON/OFF signatures. Separately check overlay draft/exact advance and the warm masking route.

summary: The installed B&W seed is suitable, but its ON/OFF pixel change alone cannot prove the guided mix was applied.
evidence: B&W enabled with Reds +40 changes 58.9%/40.9% of Canon/Sony CPU proxy pixels by over 2 display points versus bypass. Neutral monochrome would also change pixels; Reds must be nonzero to invoke the lattice guide.
proposed_fix: Keep B&W enabled and Reds +40, use the B&W eye for OFF, and use native #bw-reds drag. Verify Reds is nonzero before each ON probe. Optionally compare neutral monochrome to Reds +40 separately to isolate guide cost.
check: Both photos at Fit: B&W own eye and Reds drag plus Exposure/Contrast and Denoise probes. Check ON has guided B&W enabled and OFF disables the guide without clearing settings.

summary: The existing Vignette seed is visibly non-neutral on both photos and its percent units must be kept.
evidence: Amount −45 and Midpoint 30 moved 64.3%/62.5% of Canon/Sony CPU proxy pixels by over 2 display points. Saved Amount uses percentage units, so −45 means −0.90 EV at full coverage and −0.4 would be nearly neutral.
proposed_fix: Keep amount:-45, midpoint:30 with current midpoint scale version, the Vignette eye, and a native Amount drag. Keep Show overlay off for the baseline and exercise it only in a separate UI probe.
check: Both photos at Fit: check settled centre and corner differences between ON/OFF and confirm eye restores the seed without needing to edit recipe values.
